designSummary: Interrupted time series of weekly evening medians with segmented regression, plus descriptive fidelity and acceptance measures.
sampleSize: The line handles about 285 conversations a week, about 110 of them in evening shifts, so each weekly median is estimated from roughly 110 conversations. With 52 pre-implementation and 26 post-implementation weeks, a weekly standard deviation of about 2 minutes around the trend and lag-1 autocorrelation of 0.3, segmented regression has about 80 percent power to detect an immediate level change of 2.5 minutes at two-sided alpha 0.05; the hoped-for fall from 11 to 5 minutes is well above this. The number of weeks is fixed by the go-live date and the 26-week reporting window.
primaryAnalysis: Segmented regression of the weekly evening median time to first human reply with terms for pre-implementation trend, level change and slope change at go-live, adjusted for weekly demand and a holiday indicator, with Newey-West standard errors for autocorrelation.
secondaryAnalysis: Same model for the weekly proportion of abandoned conversations (binomial); fidelity proportions with 95 percent intervals by month; acceptability scores at weeks 8 and 24; counsellor overtime described.
missingData: Weeks with platform outages are flagged and excluded from the model with a sensitivity analysis that includes them; missing volunteer questionnaires are reported, not imputed.
multiplicity: One primary outcome; the other measures are descriptive or secondary and reported with intervals.
software: R; analysis code and outcome definitions archived before the vendor export is received.
overfittingGuards: Model terms fixed before the export
No searching for alternative change points
Covariates limited to demand and holidays
Analysis starts only after the data gate is met
summary: Seventy-eight weekly points give about 80 percent power for a 2.5-minute level change; fidelity and acceptance are descriptive.
